title: Miami Spice Back with New Reserve Tier and 300 Restaurants

whatHappening: Miami Spice Restaurant Month is returning for its 25th edition, running from August 1 through September 30, 2026. The program features three-course prix-fixe menus with at least 30% savings at more than 300 participating restaurants, and introduces a new Reserve tier this year.
whoInvolved: The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) is organizing the event, a destination marketing organization that promotes Miami as a travel and dining destination. The program brings together over 300 restaurants across Miami's diverse culinary scene.
whyMatters: Miami Spice drives significant visitor traffic and revenue during the traditionally slower summer months, benefiting both restaurants and the broader hospitality economy. articleBody:
Miami's dining scene is celebrating the return of Miami Spice Restaurant Month, the annual promotional event now in its 25th year. Running from August 1 through September 30, 2026, the program offers diners the chance to experience three-course prix-fixe menus at a minimum of 30% savings across more than 300 participating restaurants throughout the Miami area.

The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) continues to lead the initiative, which has become a signature event for the region. According to Miami Curated, this year's edition introduces a new Reserve tier, expanding the program's structure beyond its traditional format. The addition reflects growing demand from both restaurants and visitors seeking premium dining experiences at discounted prices during the slower summer season.

Miami Spice has historically served an important economic function for the hospitality industry. By promoting dining across the summer months—typically a slower travel period—the program helps restaurants maintain revenue and staffing levels while attracting visitors who might otherwise travel elsewhere. The expansion to over 300 restaurants demonstrates the program's maturation and its increasing appeal to establishments across different price points and cuisines.

The program's growth underscores Miami's position as a major culinary destination. The diversity of participating restaurants reflects the city's multicultural character, offering everything from casual to fine dining experiences. For visitors, the guaranteed 30% discount makes it an opportune time to explore neighborhoods and restaurants they might not otherwise visit, strengthening customer loyalty and discovery.

With nearly three months of programming ahead, Miami Spice aims to drive both immediate economic activity and longer-term brand recognition for the destination. The introduction of the Reserve tier signals confidence in the program's trajectory and suggests organizers are responding to market demand for tiered options that cater to different diner preferences and budgets. As the program enters its 25th year, it remains a cornerstone marketing initiative for Greater Miami's hospitality sector.

title: Where Elegance Lives: 5 Wonderful Miami Bars
summary: One of my go-to spots when I’m in New York City is the iconic King Cole Bar at the St. Regis. Stepping inside always feels like an immersion into a bygone era—a time when elegance was a deeply desired way of life. Even as modern fashion has shifted toward the casual, the bar…
whatHappening: Miami Curated has published a guide to five elegant bars in Miami, drawing inspiration from the timeless sophistication of iconic establishments like the King Cole Bar in New York City. The piece celebrates venues that preserve a sense of refined elegance even as casual fashion and culture dominate modern life.
whoInvolved: Miami Curated, a lifestyle publication focused on the Miami area, is the source. The article references the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York, a luxury hotel operated by Marriott International and known for its five-star and five-diamond ratings.
whyMatters: The piece highlights an ongoing tension between modern casual culture and traditional elegance, showing that demand persists for spaces that preserve a sophisticated atmosphere. For Miami's hospitality and leisure sectors, such guides drive tourism and establish the city's positioning as a destination for upscale dining and entertainment experiences.
articleBody:
Miami has long attracted visitors and residents seeking world-class dining and nightlife, but finding venues that marry contemporary energy with genuine elegance can prove challenging. According to Miami Curated, several bars in the city deliver that rare combination—spaces where refinement remains central to the experience rather than an afterthought. The publication's guide draws from a broader appreciation for establishments that harken back to eras when sophistication was not merely a design choice but a fundamental way of life.

The King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York exemplifies this philosophy. The historic hotel, developed by John Jacob Astor IV and completed in 1904 at the southeast corner of Fifth Avenue and East 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, has maintained its status as a landmark of American luxury hospitality for over a century. Operated by Marriott International, the St. Regis holds both Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings, testifying to its enduring commitment to excellence. Stepping into the King Cole Bar immerses visitors in an atmosphere that captures a bygone era—one where elegance was a deeply desired way of life.

Miami's bar scene increasingly reflects a similar sensibility. While contemporary culture has shifted toward casual dress and informal settings, a meaningful clientele continues to seek spaces that honor tradition, craftsmanship, and refined aesthetics. The five bars featured in Miami Curated's selection reportedly share this commitment, offering patrons an escape into environments where attention to detail, quality service, and sophisticated ambiance define the experience. These establishments serve not merely as places to drink, but as stages for a particular vision of how leisure time can be spent.

The appeal of such venues extends beyond their physical design. They represent a statement about values—a choice to preserve certain standards even when doing so requires conscious effort and investment. In an era dominated by casual dining and stripped-down interiors, bars that maintain dress codes, curate their clientele, and invest in period details or timeless design become increasingly distinctive. They offer something increasingly rare: a commitment to elegance as an intentional practice rather than an accident of décor.

For Miami's hospitality industry, this guide underscores an important market reality. Tourists and locals alike continue to seek experiences that feel elevated and purposeful, venues where the act of going out carries a sense of occasion. By identifying and celebrating bars that embody these qualities, Miami Curated validates an aesthetic approach that might otherwise feel out of step with contemporary trends. The city's ability to offer such spaces strengthens its reputation as a destination capable of serving multiple constituencies—from casual visitors to those seeking more formal, refined experiences.

articleBody:

title: From Casual Lunch to Serious Dinner: Paperfish Sushi Brickell Stepped Up Its Game
summary: Paperfish Sushi Brickell has always been one of my “go to” places to have lunch or happy hour with a friend and they always like it. With all of the sushi restaurants in town you’d ask why Paperfish Sushi? The lovely décor that brightens up your day the moment you walk in,…
whatHappening: Paperfish Sushi Brickell has elevated its offerings beyond casual lunch and happy hour fare, stepping into more ambitious dinner service territory. The Brickell sushi restaurant is expanding its appeal to diners seeking a more serious dining experience while maintaining the casual-friendly reputation that made it a neighborhood favorite.
whoInvolved: Paperfish Sushi Brickell is a sushi restaurant located in Miami's Brickell neighborhood, competing in a crowded local market of Japanese cuisine establishments. The restaurant has built its reputation as a reliable go-to spot for lunch and happy hour with a clientele that values both food quality and ambiance.
whyMatters: The restaurant's evolution reflects the competitive dynamics of Miami's dining scene, where establishments must continually innovate to retain customer loyalty and attract new demographics. By positioning itself as both a casual lunch destination and a serious dinner option, Paperfish is widening its revenue potential and customer base beyond the typical daytime and early-evening crowds.
articleBody:
Paperfish Sushi Brickell has long occupied a comfortable niche in Miami's dining landscape—the kind of place friends meet for a leisurely lunch or colleagues gather after work for happy hour. But the restaurant is now making a deliberate push upmarket, transforming itself into a destination worthy of a serious dinner reservation, not just a convenient midday stop. According to Miami Curated, the shift represents both an acknowledgment of customer demand and a strategic response to the competitive pressures facing mid-tier restaurants in South Florida.

What initially drew customers to Paperfish was a combination of reliable execution and thoughtful design. The restaurant's aesthetic—bright, welcoming décor that lifts spirits upon entry—provided an escape from the typical sushi-house formula. For casual diners, this was more than enough: a pleasant environment, competent sushi preparation, and a laid-back atmosphere justified repeat visits. The happy hour crowd especially appreciated the accessible pricing and social-friendly setting. In a market saturated with sushi options, Paperfish had carved out a defensible position.

Yet complacency is dangerous in the restaurant industry. The Brickell neighborhood continues to attract diners willing to pay premium prices for elevated experiences, and Paperfish recognized an opportunity to capture that segment. The transition from casual lunch destination to serious dinner venue requires more than menu tweaks; it demands refinement across every touchpoint—from service protocols to ingredient sourcing to the overall pacing of the meal.

The timing of this shift reflects broader patterns in Miami's post-pandemic dining recovery. Restaurants that survived on daytime and happy hour traffic have increasingly sought to build stronger dinner service revenue. For Paperfish, the move represents both a risk and an opportunity: risk because shifting identity can alienate existing customers, but opportunity because the restaurant's existing reputation for quality and ambiance provides a foundation for upscale positioning.

What remains to be seen is whether Paperfish can successfully straddle both worlds—maintaining its appeal to casual lunch crowds while building credibility among fine-dining enthusiasts. The restaurant's lovely décor and established customer loyalty provide advantages that newer fine-dining entrants lack. If execution at dinner service matches the consistency that made lunch popular, Paperfish may succeed in becoming a versatile destination for multiple occasions rather than a single-use venue.

title: PASTA: The Model Miami Restaurant
summary: Very reasonable prices, excellent food across the board, very good service, low noise decibel so you can easily talk, PASTA is a dream restaurant which should serve as a model to others in Miami. I'll even go so far as to say it has the best pasta in Miami. And on top of all…
whatHappening: PASTA, a pasta-focused restaurant in Miami, is being held up as an exemplary dining establishment that combines affordable pricing with high-quality food and service. The restaurant is earning praise for delivering an experience that other Miami venues should emulate.
whoInvolved: PASTA is a Miami-based restaurant specializing in pasta cuisine. Miami Curated, the publication reviewing the establishment, covers dining and lifestyle recommendations for Miami's restaurant scene.
whyMatters: The review suggests that PASTA demonstrates it is possible to operate a successful, high-quality restaurant in Miami's competitive dining market without excessive pricing or noise levels that compromise the dining experience. As a model for other establishments, the restaurant's approach to balancing quality, affordability, and service standards could influence how competitors approach their operations in the region.
articleBody:
A Miami restaurant is drawing attention for setting a standard that other establishments in the city should follow. According to Miami Curated, PASTA combines very reasonable prices with excellent food quality, very good service, and a notably quiet atmosphere that allows diners to converse comfortably—a rarity in the Miami dining scene.

The reviewer goes further in endorsing the establishment, even claiming that PASTA serves the best pasta in Miami. This assessment covers food across the board rather than a single signature dish, suggesting the kitchen maintains consistent quality throughout its menu offerings. The combination of these attributes—culinary excellence, affordability, attentive service, and acoustic design—positions PASTA as an outlier in a market where restaurants often prioritize one or two elements while compromising on others.

Miami's dining landscape operates within a broader context of a major metropolitan area. The city is the second-most populous city proper in Florida with 442,241 residents, and the Miami metropolitan area encompasses an estimated 6.39 million people, ranking as the fifth-largest metropolitan area in the Southeast. This scale creates both opportunity and intense competition for restaurants seeking to establish themselves as destinations worth visiting.

The emphasis on PASTA as a model suggests that many Miami restaurants may be missing opportunities by not maintaining the balance this establishment achieves. The combination of noise control and service quality, alongside culinary merit and pricing strategy, creates an experience where dining is not merely about consuming food but about enjoying an entire evening without compromise. The reviewer's recommendation carries implicit criticism of the prevailing approach in Miami's restaurant industry.

The praise for PASTA serves as a case study in how restaurants can succeed in a competitive market by attending to fundamentals: quality ingredients and preparation, fair pricing that doesn't exploit location or reputation, staff training that ensures consistent service, and even architectural or design choices that enhance rather than detract from the dining experience. Whether other Miami restaurants will follow this model remains to be seen.
